extracted.intended_audience: prospective authors submitting articles to Notices of the American Mathematical Society (professional mathematicians and STEM professionals)
extracted.subtask_short: writing for Notices of the AMS
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for authors preparing expository, news, opinion, review, and profession-related articles for Notices of the American Mathematical Society, covering suitable topics, audience expectations, submission process, and review standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal mission — exposition and news (not a research journal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices is not a research journal but rather a journal of exposition and news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices publishes high-level expository articles, AMS surveys and reports, professional-opinion pieces, community updates, and news. Submissions should aim to inform and engage a broad professional mathematics readership rather than present original research papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience — broad appeal for diverse readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices publishes articles that have broad appeal for a diverse audience with many different types of readers: graduate students, academic mathematicians, industrial mathematicians, researchers in mathematics-based fields, and amateur enthusiasts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should write at a level accessible to this mixed audience, keeping exposition clear and broadly engaging; the print edition reaches ~30,000 AMS members and the online version is freely accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topics sought — major developments, history, and professional issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices seeks exceptional articles that report on major new developments in mathematics or that describe great mathematicians or episodes from mathematics history that have connections to current research in the field. We also welcome articles discussing aspects of the mathematics profession, such as grant programs, the job market, professional opportunities for mathematicians, publishing, electronic communications, and mathematics education, at all levels. In addition, we publish reviews of books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose topics that connect to current research or the profession and will interest the Notices readership; book reviews are explicitly accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content restrictions — no offensive or inflammatory articles
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notices does not publish articles which are offensive or inflammatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid content that could be seen as offensive or inflammatory; editorial staff will reject or request revisions for submissions that violate this standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refereeing standards — technical correctness and exposition
rubrics_metrics.description: All articles are refereed for technical correctness as well as exposition, and publication is contingent on making the changes required by the referees and editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should be both technically accurate and well-explained; expect peer review and required revisions prior to publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission process — use Editflow and follow provided guidelines and template
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles should be submitted for consideration using our peer review management system Editflow. Please see this document for guidelines to use in creating your submission. A template is available for articles in LaTeX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare manuscripts according to the Notices' author guidelines and LaTeX template, and submit through Editflow; failure to follow submission guidelines may delay review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation and charges — no payment to authors and no APC
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are not paid, nor are authors asked to pay an Article Processing Charge (APC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should not expect monetary compensation and will not be billed APCs for publication in Notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation policy — solicited and unsolicited submissions welcome
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices both solicits articles and welcomes unsolicited articles for consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may submit unsolicited pieces; editors also commission content. For certain item types (e.g., features, memorial tributes, communications, opinions, reviews, news), contact the Editor-in-Chief as listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official version and availability — online version is official record
rubrics_metrics.description: The online version of Notices is freely available. The online version is the official version of record and may, on occasion, differ slightly from the print version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should be aware that the online publication is the authoritative copy and that minor differences between print and online may occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted article types and editorial contacts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Editor-in-Chief should be contacted about articles for consideration, including features, memorial tributes, communications, opinions, reviews, news about research, and news of unusual interest. The Managing Editor should be contacted for additions to Mathematics People and any corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specified editorial contacts for queries and for routing particular kinds of submissions (features, tributes, communications, opinions, reviews, news, Mathematics People, Math Calendar, Bookshelf, classifieds, advertising, permissions, letters to the editor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication frequency and distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices is a monthly that publishes 11 times a year, with a combined June/July issue. The print edition of Notices is sent to approximately 30,000 members of the AMS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan timing of submissions with awareness of the publication schedule and the wide distribution of the print edition.
